claim.summary: In the full Boolean algebra on n>=2 bits, every nonzero V<=P_<=K with K<n has dim(P_<=1 V)-dim V>=n-K, sharply. For the complete accuracy-h coordinate tuple (x1,...,xn), every K>=0 and nonzero X<=Tmap(P_<=K), Tmap f=(xi f), give displayed stable-core budget max(K+4,K+1+T*B)>=n+2, where q=min(n,dim(P_<=1 X)-dim X), T=max(1,ceil(q/h)-1), and original B>=2h+1. Equality is attained at h1,B3,K=n-2 with a monomial preimage. The actual source instead has weight x1 and a constant first row with original replay cost2h+2, hence4 at h1. This concerns that sufficient budget, not all stable-core algorithms or hard old quotients.
claim.assessment: Working leading-monomial growth calculation and all-parameter source-budget comparison. No fresh numerical sweep: the already archived three-bit affine-domain cases are consistent controls. The full Boolean base is satisfiable, and no source hardness or unconditional Frege advance is asserted.

If max(K+4delta,K+delta+T*B)<=D, one surviving old f of degree<=K+delta and simultaneous binary polynomial coefficient maps of degree<=T kill all weighted generator images, excluding degree-B PC/NS refutations. Tuple eigencharacters normalize nonzero cores and Booleanity handles zero cores; each residual rank is <=q. This does not require nested per-block cores or a unit in X. Zero Tmap image is trivial when B<=D.
